LESSON: PERIODICITY

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: CHEMISTRY FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE
Strand: Inorganic chemistry
Topic 1.5: Periodicity
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 34

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Periodicity, part of Inorganic chemistry in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 CHEMISTRY FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: Why is the study of chemical families important? 2. How does the position of an element in the periodic table influence its properties?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Periodicity together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: as the learner discusses in groups, the trends in physical properties of elements

in group I, II, VII and VIII.

● Self-efficacy: the learner confidently communicates the uses of selected elements while making presentations in

plenary

● Learning to learn: The learner independently learns by practising writing balanced chemical equations for reactions

involving group I, II and VII elements.

● Digital literacy: The learner uses digital devices with assistive technology appropriately to search for information

on the uses of group I, II, VII and VIII elements.

Values:
Unity: The learner appreciates the participation of each member of the group as they carry out experiments to investigate

physical and chemical properties of elements in the chemical families.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

● Learner Support Programmes (healthy inter and intra personal relationships): as the learner searches with peers for

information on the uses of elements in group I, II, VII and VIII.

● Socio-Economic and Environmental issues (Road safety): The learner discuss the use of selected elements in

illuminating street lights for safe roads

● Life skills (assertiveness): The learner confidently presents their findings on the uses of elements in group I, II, VII

and VIII of the periodic table

24

Suggested learning resources

Print and tactile braille version of the periodic table, 3-D models of the periodic table, plasticine, clay, braille labelling

tape, manilla papers, markers, digitals devices with assistive technology, tactile versions of lab equipment such as such

as talking scales, tactile measuring devices, adapted syringes, beakers and graduated cylinders.

Suggested Key Skill(s)

Describe trends in properties in groups and periods.
